Guides

A week, in outline

These are patterns, not prescriptions. Swap in whatever iron food and whatever allergen you are practising.

Findings

At six months the plate is small and the milk feeds stay. One or two meals, each with an iron food, are enough to begin.
At nine months texture and the allergen habit are the work. Three meals, soft pieces, and peanut or egg on several days.
At twelve months the child eats family food, unsalted on their plate. Milk becomes a drink in a cup, in a moderate amount.

Around six months

Breakfast can be oat porridge with cooked apple, and a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter stirred in once peanut has been tried. Lunch can be chicken, sweet potato, and broccoli, mashed. A second meal, if the baby wants it, can be red lentil soup or egg mashed into vegetables.

Across the week, repeat egg, peanut, wheat, and a dairy food on purpose. Keep breast milk or formula as the main drinks. Water is offered, not pushed.

Around nine months

Breakfast is porridge or egg with fruit. Lunch is a soft pasta with tomato and minced meat, or fish with rice and greens. An afternoon bite is yogurt or a soft vegetable fritter. Supper can be the family’s stew, mashed, before salt is added.

Finger foods sit beside the spoon: a strip of soft cooked pepper, a piece of ripe pear, a flake of salmon. This is the age to leave thin purée behind if you have not already.

Around twelve months

Meals look like the household’s meals. Bread and fruit at breakfast, a bean stew or a pasta at lunch, a baked egg or leftover meat in the evening. Snacks are fruit, yogurt, or a soft oat bite, not a sweet biscuit as a habit.

Honey is now legally safer regarding botulism and still a poor everyday sweetener. Whole grapes are still halved lengthways. Whole nuts are still years away. Salt can enter family food in small amounts; the child’s food does not need the adult quantity.
